newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks finish mixed after whirlwind session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks finish mixed after whirlwind session.

text.p: Wall Street stocks turned in a mixed performance after a blistering session that saw New York Stock Exchange volume hit its highest level since July.

The Dow industrials eked out a 12 point gain to close unofficially at 6485 after a tripple-witching session that saw blue chips surge more than 70 points at the open, twice triggering NYSE program trading curbs on the NYSE.
"Today's action and volatility was directly related to options expiration," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.

In contrast to yesterday, when a powerhouse rally propelled the Dow more than 126 points for its second sharpest net gain ever, the market appeared decidedly cautious, despite an opening blitz on blue chips.
"The buy side imbalances were huge at the open," Bleier said. "But Nasdaq turned around almost immediately."
Indeed, technology issues lagged the market all session.
International Business Machines Corp fell 3-1/2 to 154-5/8 and Intel Corp dipped 2-7/8 to 134-5/8.
"We saw some real profit taking today," said Joseph Battipaglia, chief investment officer at Gruntal & Co.
Volume topped 650 million shares on the NYSE for the third highest total in history and the highest since July 16, when the exchange handled a record 680.3 million shares in volume.
Volume was clearly inflated by the triple-witching expiration of stock options, index options and futures, which triggered huge position-squaring by institutions.
While investors were shying from tech stocks, they were flocking to defensive issues like banks and drug stocks.
"We saw people getting themselves positioned in classic defensive plays," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital.
The Dow's gains today brought its rise for the week to nearly 180 points, it's best week since the first full week of November, when blue chips began a scorching month-long rally.
But even so, analysts doubted the market would make much headway next week, although they said individual sectors could see action.

"We'll probably see some more rotation going into the end of the year, but we're not going to see much new money," Froehlich said. "I just think there's not a lot of demand for new stock going into next week."
Merck and Co Inc was among the strongest drug stocks, up 1-5/8 to 82-7/8. Pfizer Inc rose 5/8 to 85 and Bristol-Myers Squibb Co surged 3-1/4 to 112-1/2.
Among banks, J.P. Morgan & Co Inc rose 5/8 to 98-5/8 and Chase Manhattan Corp rose 3/4 to 91-1/2.

Coca-Cola Co was the NYSE's most active issue, jumping 1-5/8 to 52-7/8 on volume of more than 10 million shares after Salomon Brothers and Lehman Brothers both raised their ratings on the shares to buy.
Dendrite International Inc plummeted 11-1/2 to 8-1/8, a day after announcing it would lose money in its fourth quarter. Goldman Sachs downgraded the shares to market perform this morning.

Redhook Ale Brewery Inc tumbled 4-5/8 to 9-3/8. The company said yesterday its fourth quarter results would be below expectations and today investment firm Piper Jaffray downgraded the company to market performer from strong buy.
The S&P 500 rose 3.11 to 748.87.
The NYSE Composite rose 1.95 to 394.11
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
